content: Benzyl acetate, identified by the CAS number 140-11-4, is an organic compound with the molecular formula C9H10O2. It is classified as an ester, which is formed through the condensation reaction between benzyl alcohol and acetic acid. This compound occurs naturally in a variety of flowers and is a major component of the essential oils derived from jasmine, ylang-ylang, and tobira flowers. Benzyl acetate is characterized by a pleasant, sweet aroma that closely resembles the scent of jasmine. Due to this aromatic property, it is extensively utilized in the production of perfumes and cosmetics. Additionally, it is employed in flavoring agents to impart apple and pear-like flavors. Benzyl acetate is also known to attract male orchid bees of various species. These bees collect the compound, presumably to synthesize pheromones. This property makes benzyl acetate a common bait used in the study and collection of orchid bees. Furthermore, benzyl acetate serves as a solvent in a range of industrial applications. It is used in the processing of plastics and resins, as well as in cellulose acetate, cellulose nitrate, oils, lacquers, polishes, and inks.
